title: Commercial Arithmetic: Profit, Loss, Simple Interest, Discount and Commission

standard_text: Solve problems on money: profit and loss, simple interest, discount and commission; calculate profit and loss per cent. (summary of the NERDC Primary 5 Mathematics curriculum)
meta_desc: Free Primary 5 maths worksheets on money in naira: profit and loss, profit per cent, simple interest, discount and commission. 100 questions with answers.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Profit = selling price − cost price. Loss = cost price − selling price.
  • Profit per cent = profit ÷ cost price × 100.
  • Simple interest I = P × R × T ÷ 100, where P is the principal, R the rate per cent and T the time in years.
  • A discount is money taken off the marked price. A commission is a part of the sales paid to the seller.

Examples

Example

Interest on ₦50,000 at 8% for 3 years

50,000 × 8 × 3 ÷ 100

Answer: ₦12,000

Example

10% discount on ₦25,000

25,000 ÷ 10 = 2,500

Answer: Pay ₦22,500

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Dividing by the selling price for profit per centAlways divide by the cost price.
Forgetting to add the interest to get the amountAmount = principal + interest.
Giving the discount instead of the price to payPrice to pay = marked price − discount.

faq.a: Agents and sales people, on what they sell.

items.q: Kunle bought a school bag for ₦11,250 and sold it for ₦13,150. Did he make a profit or a loss, and how much?
items.e: Selling price > cost price, so it is a profit: ₦13,150 − ₦11,250 = ₦1,900.
